_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), set 31/4/1 (Series D4CBA/4), opener of series 31/4: nothing skipped (plan.txt lists no reference). 27 page images, idx 0-26 (cover announces 27 printed pages; last folio 27 on idx 26). idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions + Q1-2; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-26 (each odd index is the Hindi of the page after it); odd-page tops checked, all Hindi, and every English page ends on a complete question, so no English overflows onto an odd page; idx 26 (last page) is English Q39. Instructions (i)-(vii) confirm sci80: 39 questions, A Q1-20 MCQ @1, B Q21-26 @2, C Q27-33 @3, D Q34-36 @5, E Q37-39 case-based @4. Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (ms idx 2-7) for a bare OR: after Q21, 23, 29, 34, 35, 36, 37(c), 38(c), 39(c) = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. The scheme's other 'or's (Q28 oxidising agents, Q36(b)(ii) lens formula) sit inside an answer and are not question alternatives. Internal choices are labelled lower-case (a)/(b) and case studies (a), (b), (c)(i) OR (c)(ii), so refs follow 31/1/1's style. The 8-page scheme block is COMPLETE: general instructions on ms idx 0-1, then every question Q1-Q39 answered on ms idx 2-7, ending with Q39(c)(ii). All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme page image (ms idx 2); each was re-derived and 19 agree; Q17 disagrees (flagged, CBSE's B kept). No void note on any MCQ; one award-regardless note on Q37(b) (see that row). Decimal points on this paper are RAISED dots (Q13 0·5 Ω, Q25 4·0, Q26 0·2 mm, Q36 table 37·5), written {\cdot}.

questions._flag: KEY DISAGREEMENT, CBSE's (B) kept. Re-derived as (C): NCERT says roasting converts sulphide ores into OXIDES ('2ZnS + 3O2 -> 2ZnO + 2SO2'; even for HgS and Cu2S the roasting step gives the oxide, and the metal comes from a later reduction), so the Reason 'Roasting converts sulphide ores directly into metals' is false. questions.stem:
1 gram of solid sodium chloride was taken in a clean and dry test tube and concentrated sulphuric acid was added to it.

(i) Name the gas evolved in the reaction.

(ii) What will be observed when this gas is tested with (I) dry, and (II) wet blue litmus paper ? Write your conclusion about the nature (acidic/basic) of this gas.
Some metals react with acids to produce salt and hydrogen gas. Illustrate it with an example. How will you test the presence of this gas ?
Distinguish between a saturated and an unsaturated hydrocarbon by flame test. List the products of combustion reaction of a saturated hydrocarbon.
We need to water the soil in plants on a regular basis. But it ultimately reaches the leaves of the plant. Explain how this takes place.
Name the type of nutrition exhibited by Amoeba. Explain how food is taken in and digested by this organism.
The survival of a species is promoted through creation of variations. Illustrate with an example.

questions.stem:
A student fixes a sheet of white paper on a drawing board. He places a bar magnet in the centre of it. He sprinkles some iron filings uniformly around the bar magnet. Then he taps the drawing board gently and observes that the iron filings arrange themselves in a particular pattern.

(a) Why do iron filings arrange in a particular pattern ?

(b) What does the crowding of iron filings at the ends of the magnet indicate ?

(c) What do the lines, along which the iron filings align, represent ?

(d) If the student places a cardboard horizontally in a current carrying solenoid and repeats the above activity, in what pattern would the iron filings arrange ? State the conclusion drawn about the magnetic field based on the observed pattern of the lines.

questions._flag: Tests what a chemical reaction is and the observable signs of one (the NCERT chapter introduction, before section 1.1); no subtopic covers that, so filed on the chapter's first section, as 2025 31/4/1 Q1 was. Name wanted: 'Recognising Chemical Reactions'.
questions.stem: What is a chemical reaction ? Describe one activity each to show that a chemical change has occurred in which (i) change of colour, and (ii) change in temperature has taken place.

(i) Define a decomposition reaction. How can we say that (I) electrolysis of water, and (II) blackening of silver bromide when exposed to sunlight, are decomposition reactions ? Mention the type of energy involved in each case.

(ii) “The type of reactions in which (I) calcium oxide is formed, and (II) calcium hydroxide is formed are opposite reactions to each other.” Justify this statement with the help of chemical equations.

questions.stem:
(i) Define a reflex arc. Why have reflex arcs evolved in animals ? Trace the sequence of events which occur, when you suddenly touch a hot object.

(ii) Name the part of nervous system which helps in communication between the central nervous system and other parts of the body. What are the two components of this system ?

(i) Leaves of ‘chhui-mui’ plant begin to fold up and droop in response to a stimulus. Name the stimulus and write the cause for such a rapid movement. Is there any growth involved in the movement ?

(ii) Define geotropism in plants. What is meant by positive and negative geotropism ? Give one example of each type.

The variation of image distance (v) with object distance (u) for a convex lens is given in the following observation table. Analyse it and answer the questions that follow :

| S. No. | Object distance (u) cm | Image distance (v) cm |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | \(-150\) | \(+30\) |
| 2 | \(-75\) | \(+37{\cdot}5\) |
| 3 | \(-50\) | \(+50\) |
| 4 | \(-37{\cdot}5\) | \(+75\) |
| 5 | \(-30\) | \(+150\) |
| 6 | \(-15\) | \(+37{\cdot}5\) |

(i) Without calculation, find the focal length of the convex lens. Justify your answer.

(ii) Which observation is not correct ? Why ? Draw ray diagram to find the position of the image formed for this position of the object.

(iii) Find the approximate value of magnification for \(u = -30\) cm.
